en: The Scripture on the One-Syllable King of Mantras from the Dharani Treasury of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Yijing by Imperial Command during the Tang Dynasty.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha was in the Heaven of Pure Abodes,
sitting cross-legged among the celestial hosts with right mindfulness.
Surveying the great assembly, he addressed them, saying:
"O sons of the gods,
you should listen with a sincere mind to the subtle and wondrous conduct of the youth Mañjuśrī."
This is the ritual procedure for the mantra of the maṇḍala deities,
the foremost secret and supreme heart-mantra required for healing illnesses and protecting the body.
This great king of mantras is proclaimed and praised by all Tathāgatas.
If there are good sons or good daughters [who uphold it]...
Whoever is able to recite this mantra is thereby upholding all divine mantras.
You, O assembly of devas!
This great king of mantras cannot be contravened by anyone.
Even if it were Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
this mantra could still draw him forth and bring him under its power according to one's will.
It causes messengers to appear before one to perform all manner of tasks;
how much more so for all other bodhisattvas and all mundane and supramundane divine mantras.
All obstacles are entirely dispelled;
it possesses great valor and great majestic power,
with its spiritual efficacy being foremost.
This single syllable is the most supreme among all mantras and the most honored among all characters.
This one syllable is capable of accomplishing all undertakings and can bring all wholesome dharmas to complete perfection.
It is eternally present throughout all mundane and supramundane realms;
it stands above all incantations and cannot be destroyed.
It is the heart-mind of all Buddhas.
It is able to fulfill all requests and aspirations.
You hosts of devas,
listen with single-minded attention to this inconceivable, most supreme divine mantra of great majestic power.
He then spoke the mantra:
Oṃ chlohe yan. These four characters form a single word; therefore, both the Sanskrit and Chinese forms are preserved. You hosts of devas!
This is the supreme one-syllable king of mantras among all secrets.
No sentient being dares to transgress it,
and no ghosts or spirits dare to approach it.
All Buddhas regard it as an auspicious matter;
among all mantras, it is most capable of accomplishing whatever one intends;
and within all worlds, it acts as the greatest sovereign.
It possesses great mastery over those who seek wealth, enabling them to become prosperous;
among all forms of ill-will, it renders them charitable and kind;
and its nature is one of compassion for all sentient beings.
Those who were rebellious all became submissive. In short,
whatever they undertook was entirely successful.
Even if one does not perform the ritual procedures such as entering the maṇḍala, but simply recites and maintains the mantra,
when one touches that [object] with the hand, it immediately becomes available for use at will.
When wearing the enchanted garment, [the same applies].
All people love and delight in seeing him, and those who behold him rejoice. If one uses a tooth-stick while reciting this mantra to clean the teeth, any toothache will be immediately cured.
If one suffers from eye ailments, [the same applies].
Take saindhava salt and grind it into a powder.
After reciting the mantra seven times, place a small amount into the eye;
the pain will then cease.
If one suffers from ear ailments,
take earth fungi from a heap of elephant or horse dung,
along with sesame oil and siddhārtha salt.
Take a small amount of each, recite the mantra over them seven times,
grind them together in one place until they are finely crushed, squeeze out the juice, and warm it.
Drop it into the ear canal, and the pain will immediately cease.
If there is a woman who,
at the time of childbirth,
is afflicted by the fetal membrane and suffers from constricting pains within her womb such that she cannot deliver quickly;
Take the root of *aṭarūṣaka* or the root of *śatāvarī*.
Grind them with water free of insects until they are finely crushed.
Recite the mantra over them seven times and apply it below the navel.
One will then be able to emerge easily.
If a person is struck by an arrow and the shaft enters the body but cannot be extracted, [this mantra shall be applied].
One may take aged clarified butter and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times;
if one causes the patient to drink it, the arrowhead will emerge.
If one suffers from indigestion of long-standing food, [the same applies].
For those who suffer from knots and pains in the abdomen, with symptoms shifting between upward distress and downward diarrhea, and who are delirious and fear death,
one should take black salt (*kālalavaṇa*), or *saindhava* salt, or various other types of salt,
and recite the mantra over them seven times.
Grind [the ingredients] into a powder and administer with warm water;

the illness will be cured immediately. Alternatively, for those suffering from severe dysentery that cannot be stopped, take the roots of the mandarin orange (*citrus reticulata*), the pomelo (*citrus maxima*), and the *míngzhā* (*dillenia indica*).
Grind and pound it, reciting the mantra seven times over it.
Dissolve it in water and drink it, and one will immediately recover.
If this is a "stone woman" (a woman unable to give birth), there is no method for delivery.
For those who seek to obtain a son or daughter,
one should take the root of the aśvagandhā plant,
boil it thoroughly with clarified butter, and then crush it into a paste.
Recite the *Go-rasa-mantra* twenty-five times over buffalo milk.
Once the woman’s body has been purified, have her drink the medicine. [Tell her:
"Wife, do not violate another man."
Now, she had never violated another woman.
Not long after, she became pregnant;
yet, there were also women who had severed their lineage and were childless.
After three or five years, or even many more years,
they may be subject to the prohibitions and incantations of others,
or due to malevolent sorcery, or because of various illnesses, or being harassed by others, or encountering toxic drugs.
If one encounters such adverse conditions and consequently has no offspring,
one should take a small amount of peacock tail feathers and place them in aged ghee,
boiling them for as many times as there are arrows.
Grind them until they are well blended.
Add a small amount of rock honey, about the size of a jujube fruit,
and recite the mantra twenty-seven times before consuming it entirely.
For the next seven days, she took milk mixed with rock sugar every day,
reciting the mantra over it seven times each time before drinking it.
Her female body became pure, all her ailments were cured, and she immediately conceived.
If there is a woman whose menstrual flow does not cease,
one should take a handful of *ālabu* root or blue lotus root, pound it, mix it with milk,
and boil it thoroughly; after reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, she should drink it and will immediately be cured.
If one suffers from a headache,
one should recite the mantra over a raven feather seven times and sweep it over the painful area; the ailment will then be cured forever.
If a person suffers from malaria that recurs every day, every two days, every three days, or every four days;
or from a chronic fever, or a temporary fever.
One should mix milk gruel with ghee and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times;
upon consuming it, the ailment will immediately be cured.
If a person has been struck by the malevolent charms, sorcery, or toxic poisons of others, [the same shall apply].
One should perform the counter-contemplation and recite the mantra over one's own face one hundred and eight times;
by contemplating the patient in this way, their ailment will immediately be cured.
If a person is possessed by malevolent spirits such as the kṛtya-putana and other ghosts,
or suffers from various ailments of children,
or is otherwise afflicted by any non-human beings acting together to cause distress;
One should recite the mantra over one's own hand one hundred and eight times;
by rubbing it on the patient's head, all illnesses will be cured.
If a person has been bitten by a snake or a scorpion, or wounded by a mad dog, [the same applies].
Blow the breath forcefully upon the sore and recite the mantra seven times seven; it will be cured immediately.
If there are those afflicted by leprosy or wasting diseases, [the same shall apply].
One should bathe and purify oneself in a secluded and quiet place;
by constantly reciting this mantra, all ailments will be completely cured.
This applies to anyone who recites the mantra.
One must always remain far removed from evil people and impure, foul places; do not approach alcohol, meat, or the five pungent herbs.
If one single-mindedly upholds [this practice], there will be no lack of efficacy.
If one recites it once daily for a period of one day, [the benefits will follow].
It can protect oneself;
if recited twice, it can protect one's companions;
if recited thrice, it can protect an entire household.
If one recites it four times, one can protect a single village;
if one recites it five times, one can protect a single city;
if one recites it one hundred times, one can protect an entire kingdom.
If one recites it a thousand times, one can protect the four continents.
To summarize briefly, its benefits are such as healing illnesses,
protecting the body, and providing timely assistance.
If there are any other matters to be accomplished,
they shall all be performed according to one's wishes and none shall fail to succeed.
At that time, the great assembly of devas, having heard this Sūtra of the King of One-Syllable Mantras spoken by the Buddha, [rejoiced].

Rejoice and practice with devotion. Furthermore, if there are those who aspire to seek liberation, who hope for great benefit, and who desire to realize the fruit in this very life, they should, with a sincere heart, rely upon the *dhāraṇī-piṭaka* to perform the great dhāraṇī rites as extensively explained in the sūtras.
The Sūtra on the King of One-Syllable Dhāraṇīs Spoken by the Buddha
